gates.proposition: South Base triangulation station existed by the 1904 magnetic occupation referenced in the 1908 and 1909 C&GS station descriptions.
evidence: 1908 C&GS magnetic station description states the 1904 station was reoccupied between Morro Lighthouse and South Base triangulation station, 20 paces from South Base.
1909 C&GS report states observations were made 50 feet from South Base triangulation station toward Morro Lighthouse, within a few feet of the 1904/1908 point.
gates.effect: Existence by 1904 is verified. This does not establish the original construction/occupation year.

gates.proposition: South Base triangulation station is not the 1904/1908 magnetic observation point and is not the separately monumented 1909 magnetic station.
evidence: The magnetic point is described by offset from South Base.
The 1909 point was independently monumented with a cement stone marked U.S.C.&G.S., 1909.
gates.effect: Never transfer a magnetic-station coordinate/mark to South Base without an explicit tie computation.

gates.proposition: The true bearing from the South Base vicinity toward Morro Lighthouse was N 37°09.4′ E.
gates.evidence: C&GS 1909 magnetic station description says the bearing was determined from triangulation.
gates.effect: Provides an orientation constraint but not a unique coordinate.

gates.proposition: A 1936 U.S. Engineer Office, Puerto Rico District map explicitly labels STA. SOUTH BASE.

source.publication: U.S. Serial Set / U.S. Engineer Office, Puerto Rico District, Oct. 1936

limits: The map label proves continued cartographic recognition of the station name in 1936.
The exact plotted grid coordinate has not yet been extracted from a verified image/scan.
A 1936 label does not prove establishment date or original station mark.
gates.effect: Adds a later independent cartographic survival anchor.

gates.target: Recover the 1936 map image at sufficient resolution, identify its grid reference/system, and read or derive the plotted South Base coordinate with an uncertainty budget.
gates.rejection_rule: Do not infer a precise coordinate solely from OCR fragments or a low-resolution text extraction.

gates.proposition: Hodgkins surveyed San Juan Harbor in April 1899 and a C&GS San Juan Harbor map dated 1899 survives.
limits: No inspected 1899 source yet nominates South Base by name.
Local survey control is plausible but South Base establishment in 1899 remains unproven.
gates.effect: 1899 remains a plausible local-control origin branch.

gates.proposition: Stehman Forney led triangulation from Ponce to San Juan between January and May 1900.
limits: The assignment record does not say whether South Base was established, first occupied, or reoccupied.
Network integration in 1900 remains stronger than exact establishment in 1900.

model: 1899: Hodgkins local San Juan Harbor survey/control — possible establishment context.
1900: Forney Ponce→San Juan triangulation — strong integration/occupation context.
1904: South Base demonstrably exists as triangulation reference for magnetic work.
gates.effect: Do not collapse establishment, integration, and later reoccupation into a single unsupported date.

gates.record_group: RG 23 — Records of the Coast and Geodetic Survey
target_series: GH — Horizontal and Vertical Angle Observations, 1817–1948
Records relating to surveys in insular possessions, 1900–1906
gates.effect: Original station description and first-observation evidence have a defined archival search path.

gates.target: Locate the original GA-series station description for South Base, San Juan.
required_fields: original latitude/longitude or linked computation identifier

gates.close_rule: Requires an original station description, field/reconnaissance record, computation sheet, or equivalent primary record that nominates South Base.

gates.target: Recover original coordinate, datum, monument/mark description, witness ties and first observation.
gates.close_rule: Do not backfill from the 1904/1908/1909 magnetic offsets.

gates.target: Reconcile South Base with a modern NGS station record/PID using station history, recovery notes, coordinates and monument identity.
gates.close_rule: Name similarity or spatial proximity alone is insufficient.

next_actions: Recover a high-resolution 1936 Corps map image and solve its grid coordinate for STA. SOUTH BASE.
Search GA/GAR/GH/AA and insular-possession records for South Base / San Juan / Morro / Forney / Hodgkins, 1899–1904.
Use the resulting approximate coordinate to query modern NGS control spatially, then require recovery-history identity before PID reconciliation.
